issues.legal_issue: A pleading may be amended to correct the description of disputed property when the correction is needed to bring the real controversy before the court, notwithstanding that the applicant did not seek it promptly, with prejudice to the opposing party addressed by costs.
material_facts: The plaint described a substantially larger area than the area the plaintiff later said was actually in dispute, and the proposed amendment corrected the property description.

The defendants had challenged the description in their written statement and during related proceedings, but the plaintiff sought amendment later and had maintained the original description in the meantime.
The Supreme Court considered the case factually close to an earlier decision allowing correction of a property description despite the plaintiff’s lack of promptness.
The defendants said they had suffered an injunction concerning property they owned, and the Court considered that the resulting prejudice could be met by an order for costs.
issues.conclusion: The proposed amendment to the plaint was allowed subject to payment of costs to the defendants.
issues.legal_principle: Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as amended, restricts amendments after commencement of trial unless the party could not have raised the matter earlier despite due diligence. The Court did not decide the broader question of when trial commences; it followed Sajjan Kumar v. Ram Kishan, (2005) 13 SCC 89, which allowed correction of a property description despite the plaintiff’s lack of diligence where the amendment was needed to bring out the real controversy and refusal could create complications at execution. Baldev Singh v. Manohar Singh, (2006) 6 SCC 498, and Ajendraprasadji N. Pandey v. Swami Keshavprakeshdasji, (2006) 12 SCC 1, were considered in relation to commencement of trial, but the Court made no ruling on that broader issue here.

rule.if: civil_appeal_from_amendment_denial and property_description_correction_needed and amendment_clarifies_real_dispute and prejudice_can_be_addressed_by_costs

predicates.civil_appeal_from_amendment_denial: A party appeals in a civil proceeding after a court has refused an application to amend a pleading.
predicates.property_description_correction_needed: The applicant seeks to correct the description of property identified in the pleading as the subject of the dispute.
predicates.amendment_clarifies_real_dispute: The proposed correction brings the actual disputed property or controversy into clearer focus.
predicates.prejudice_can_be_addressed_by_costs: Any prejudice to the opposing party from allowing the correction can be addressed by requiring the applicant to pay costs.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns refusal to correct a property description, and the correction clarifies the real dispute while any prejudice can be addressed by costs, the amendment is allowed subject to costs.

issues.legal_issue: The merits of a proposed pleading amendment are not determinative of whether permission to amend should be granted when the opposing party can raise its objections in a responsive pleading.
material_facts: The defendants argued that the proposed correction would materially change the property in suit and the cause of action, making the suit non-maintainable.

The Court stated that the merits of the amendment were hardly relevant to allowing the application and that the defendants could raise their objections through corresponding amendments to their written statement.
issues.conclusion: The defendants remained free to raise their objections to the amended plaint in their written statement; the asserted effect on the merits did not prevent permission to amend.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the question whether an amendment should be permitted is distinct from the merits of the amended pleading. The opposing party may raise objections to the amendment by making corresponding amendments to its written statement.

predicates.amendment_application_in_civil_suit: A party applies to amend a pleading in a civil suit.
predicates.opponent_alleges_amendment_changes_claim: The opposing party contends that the proposed amendment changes the subject matter or basis of the claim.
predicates.opponent_can_raise_objections_in_respons: The opposing party can state its objections in a responsive pleading.

issues.definition: When an opponent says an amendment changes the claim but can raise objections in a responsive pleading, the amendment’s merits do not determine whether permission is granted.
